# Turn a casual selfie into a clean LinkedIn headshot with one Gemini prompt

> **In short:** Open Gemini, upload one casual selfie, and paste a single prompt that asks for a clean LinkedIn-style headshot with a plain background. The image you get back is AI-generated, so use it as a starting point, not a final portrait.

You have a decent selfie on your phone and a LinkedIn profile that still shows a logo, an old vacation photo, or no photo at all. The good news: Google's Gemini (the AI assistant that lives at gemini.google.com and in the Gemini mobile app) can take that one casual photo and reimagine it as a tidy headshot with a simple background, in roughly the time it takes to boil water. This guide gives you a copy-paste prompt and walks you through every click.

## Before you start

- A **Google account** (the same one you use for Gmail or YouTube).
- The **Gemini app** on your phone, or the **gemini.google.com** website on a computer. Both work the same way for this task.
- **One clear selfie** — face the camera, even lighting, no sunglasses, nothing covering your face. A simple background in the selfie helps.
- About **5–10 minutes** total.
- **Heads-up:** image generation in Gemini may sit behind a paid plan depending on your region and account. The free tier usually offers a small number of image generations per day. If you hit a limit, you'll see a message in the chat saying so.

> ⚠️ **What this guide can — and cannot — do.** Gemini can generate a *new* image based on your selfie, but it is still an AI creation, not a real photo. It will not look identical to you, and it may slightly change your face, hair, or features. Treat the result as a polished starting point, and check your platform's rules before uploading it as your official headshot.

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and start a new chat

Open the Gemini app on your phone, or go to **gemini.google.com** in a browser. If you are not signed in, the page will ask you to sign in with your Google account first. Once you are in, look for a **"New chat"** button — usually at the top-left of the screen, sometimes a **pencil or plus icon** instead. Tap it so you begin with a clean conversation. You'll see an empty chat box ready for you.

💬 Example: you don't need to type anything yet in this step — just make sure the chat is empty.

You'll know it worked when you see a blank chat screen with a text box at the bottom labeled something like **"Ask Gemini"** or **"Message Gemini"**.

## Step 2 — Attach your selfie

Look for a small **paperclip**, **plus (+),** or **image icon** near the chat box. Tap it and choose **"Upload from device"** (or "Photos" on a phone). Pick the selfie you want to use. After a moment, a small thumbnail of your photo appears inside the chat box, next to where you will type. If you see a camera icon instead, tap that — it works the same way.

💬 Example: choose a single, recent photo where your face is clearly visible.

You'll know it worked when your selfie shows up as a small preview inside the message area, before you've typed anything.

## Step 3 — Paste the headshot prompt

Now click into the text box and paste the prompt below. The wording matters: it tells Gemini what kind of image to make, what kind of background to use, and that you want a head-and-shoulders crop (the kind LinkedIn prefers). Do not edit the wording yet — paste it as-is for your first try, then adjust later.

💬 Example (copy the whole block):

```
Look at the attached selfie. Generate a new image of me as a professional
LinkedIn headshot. Keep my face, hair color, and general appearance the same.
Use a soft, even studio light, a plain light gray background, and frame me
from the chest up. I am wearing a simple, neutral top. The photo should look
clean, friendly, and suitable for a public profile picture.
```

You'll know it worked when Gemini starts generating — you'll see a small spinner, then a loading bar, and finally the new image appears in the chat.

## Step 4 — Check the result and ask for small fixes

Look at the image Gemini created. Most of the time, the first try is close but not perfect: the background might be too dark, the crop too tight, or the lighting too harsh. Tell Gemini what to change in plain words. Type a short follow-up right under the image — no need to re-upload your selfie, the original is still attached to the chat.

💬 Example: *"Make the background a bit lighter."* or *"Crop a little closer to my shoulders and brighten the face."*

You'll know it worked when Gemini replies with a fresh image that matches your request. If it looks great on the first try, you can skip this step and move on.

## Step 5 — Download the image you like

When you have a version you want to keep, tap the **generated image** to open it full size. Look for a **download icon** (usually a downward arrow ⬇) or a **⋯ menu** with a **"Download"** or **"Save image"** option. On a phone, the image will save to your Photos or Gallery. On a computer, it will download to your Downloads folder. Pick the version you actually like — Gemini keeps every generation in the same chat.

💬 Example: if you tried several variations, scroll back through the chat and download the best one, not just the last one.

You'll know it worked when you find the image file in your Photos app or Downloads folder, ready to upload.

## Step 6 — Upload to LinkedIn (or your platform of choice)

Open the LinkedIn app or website, go to your profile, and tap the **camera icon** on your current profile photo. Choose **"Change photo"** and select the downloaded headshot. Crop it so your face is centered and the frame matches LinkedIn's circle. Save, and you're done. The same image works for any other platform that needs a profile picture — Gmail, Slack, X, or your company's staff page.

💬 Example: if LinkedIn shows a square preview, leave a little space above your head so the circle crop doesn't cut your hair off.

You'll know it worked when your new headshot appears on your profile and the old photo is replaced.

## Common mistakes

- **Wearing sunglasses, a hat, or a face covering in the original selfie.** The AI has trouble rebuilding features it can't see. Take a quick new selfie in even indoor light before you start.
- **Asking for too many things at once in the prompt.** "Office background, formal suit, holding a coffee cup, cinematic lighting" tends to confuse the result. Start simple, then add one change at a time in Step 4.
- **Uploading a group photo or a very small thumbnail.** Gemini needs a clear, single face to work with. Crop the photo first on your phone, or pick a different selfie.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** any time you need a profile picture fast — for a new app account, a club signup, a community forum — you can run the same prompt with a slightly different background color and have a clean photo in minutes.
- **For your business or work:** a tidy headshot helps your LinkedIn, your email signature, your company's "About Us" page, or a conference speaker bio. You can also make two versions — one with a soft gray background, one with a soft blue — to match different brand colors.
- **If you're just getting started:** the easiest first move is to try the prompt exactly as written in Step 3, on whatever selfie you already have. Even a rough first attempt teaches you how Gemini responds to specific words like "studio light" and "plain background."

## Try it now

Open Gemini right now and paste the prompt from Step 3 with any selfie you have on your phone. Spend two minutes on the first result, then send one short follow-up like *"softer light, lighter background"* to see how a small change shifts the whole image. You'll have a headshot by the time your coffee is ready.
